newsitem.title: UK: LME aluminium perky in pre-market, copper sideways.
newsitem.headline: LME aluminium perky in pre-market, copper sideways.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) aluminium and zinc took a stab at the upside in early inter-office trade on Thursday, while copper moved indecisively sideways after a stock rise.
An early bout of bank buying helped push aluminium to the $1,600 level, encouraged by the metal's positive Wednesday close and 3,450-tonne LME stock draw.
Three months metal was last at $1,601, up $9 from the previous kerb close.

"Sentiment has changed slightly to the upside. But it has to retake $1,610 before it can head up to $1,635/$40," a dealer said, adding that business was brisk early on but then returned to normal levels.
Copper was less buoyant, last indicated at $2,475/$2,479, versus $2,478, after an LME stocks rise of 250 tonnes.

Prices needed to convincingly hurdle $2,485 to trigger stops and then tackle the all-important $2,500 level, analysts said. Prices had edged up to $2,487 from a low of $2,465 in the morning before drifting lower.
But a continuation of this week's downward correction, with $2,445 as an eventual target, was probably more likely.
"With copper stocks having eneded their downard trend, and the spreads unwinding the possiblity of futher losses seems high," brokers GNI said in a commentary.
"The real question is whether the prices of the other metals can maintain independence in the wake of a copper-led sell off."
Cash to threes backwardation was barely wider at $58/$63, compared to $55/$60 at Wednesday's close.
Zinc, followed by lead, extended Wednesday's shortcovering gains after surviving a battering earlier this week.
It was last at $1,360/63, versus $1,350, and the market woudl target the recent high of $1,370 on the upside.
Lead was firmer at $630/32, from $626, with next resistance seen at $640.
Nickel, however, slipped below Wednesday's $7,200 close to $7,150/70, despite the ongoing strike at Inco's Sudbury operations.
"While the strike has limited the downside, Inco clearly has sufficient stocks to meet demand without drawing on the LME for a while yet," GNI said.
Tin was at $5,605/$5,625 from $5,600, and alloy was little changed at $1475/$1,485 versus $1,480.
